verdicts.claim: gathererLifecycle.ts:559-563 — the S161 OPEN-3 preempt calls the same function and is 'the only oscillation surface the fix opens — the `cand.type === wanted` guard is what bounds it'
verdicts.note: ⛔ THE SINGLE BIGGEST MISS. The lines are verbatim, but the bound is wrong. `cand.type === wanted` bounds oscillation only while `wanted` is STABLE — which it is today, because q[rank] changes only when the queue changes. The fix makes `wanted` a function of quarry MEMBERSHIP, which changes whenever any spark is claimed, expires (FREE_SPARK_TTL_TICKS 600) or spawns. That is verbatim the trigger the Council rejected in S141: gathererLifecycle.ts:305-307 — 'that set changes every time ANY of the player's gatherers claims a spark or deposits, so a unit that was rank 0 becomes rank 1 next tick, retargets, and can thrash indefinitely without ever completing a haul.' The fix keeps `rank` stable and makes the ENTRY IT MAPS TO unstable instead — functionally the same thrash. Worked case: 3 gatherers, queue [Square, Triangle, Circle], Squares present -> g0 Square / g1 Triangle / g2 Circle. Squares run out -> satisfiable = [Triangle, Circle] -> g1's wanted flips Triangle->Circle, `current.type !== wanted`, the preempt at :560 fires and it abandons a live Triangle mid-walk. A Square respawns -> it flips back. And this is not theoretical: constants.ts:747-748 records the MEASURED standing pool as 'solo mean 8.92 median 10' but 'bots mean 4.48 median 2 (4 gatherers consuming)' — in a bot match the satisfiable list churns on most ticks. The fix needs either a stability rule (do not re-derive `wanted` for a gatherer already committed to a live target) or a latched type on the Gatherer — and a latch is a new serialized+hashed Gatherer field (save.ts:2584/2598, stateHashFull.ts:367/609), i.e. a four-sites obligation and a size escalation the report does not carry.

The queue is not abandoned — it is served in arrival order instead of in the player's order. Minor, but the brief should say it precisely or the fix's success criterion gets mis-stated.

net_assessment:
THE DIAGNOSIS IS SOUND AND THE FIX SHAPE IS MOSTLY RIGHT. I opened every cited line. Every production-code quote is verbatim and means what the report says, the four-sites analysis is complete and correct, the no-PROTOCOL-bump conclusion holds for the no-latch variant, the host-only claim is real (main.ts:2725 `} else if (!isClient) {`, protocol.ts:1391 "GATHERER_TICK is host-internal"), and the "is there a random in it? NO" answer to the owner is correct — I re-derived the `better` truth table at :405-409 myself rather than accept it. `reproduced: CONFIRMED_IN_CODE` stands. This is not a "already fixed" or "owner was wrong" result.

THREE THINGS WOULD HAVE COST THE BRANCH, AND TWO OF THEM ARE THE EXACT S182 FAILURE SHAPES THIS LANE WAS SPAWNED FOR.

1. THE OSCILLATION BOUND IS REFUTED, AND IT IS THE S141 COUNCIL REJECTION WEARING A NEW HAT. The report says the `cand.type === wanted` guard at :563 bounds the preempt. It bounds it only while `wanted` is stable. The fix makes `wanted` a function of quarry membership, and gathererLifecycle.ts:305-307 records that BOTH external Council seats rejected the original design for depending on a set that "changes every time ANY of the player's gatherers claims a spark or deposits". Claiming a spark sets escrow and removes it from `isHarvestable` — the identical trigger. The rank stays stable and the entry it maps to starts churning instead. With constants.ts:748 measuring a bot-match pool of "mean 4.48 median 2 (4 gatherers consuming)" against six types, this fires constantly. A branch that ships the report as written re-introduces, from the other end, the precise defect the S141 Council fix exists to prevent — and its own new tests would not catch it, because they are all single-snapshot assertions with no multi-tick churn.

2. A GREEN GUARD OVER A LIVE LIE. shapeStrip.ts:170-173 quotes owner ruling B4 and states that first-appearance order is what keeps "leftmost is next" true and stops the display "lying about what happens next". The fix falsifies that sentence for most of a bot match. The test that pins it (gathererOrders.test.ts:333) exercises `coalesceOrders` in isolation and stays green throughout. Source-text/unit guard proves the function is correct; it cannot prove the head is what the gatherer fetches. Verbatim S182 §2.

3. A TOLERANT DEFAULT AND THE TWO FULL-LOOP FIXTURES BEHIND IT. The report contains the word "bot" zero times. botBrain.ts:711 reads the queue through `?? []`, bots really do emit the intent (botController.ts:279), and botTowers.test.ts:362 — whose docblock says gatherer steering is one of three causes of its greenness and that it is "kept un-weakened as the regression guard for all three" — plus firstTowerSpeed.test.ts's first-tower timing gates are both absent from file_set. In a parallel split, a branch that does not know those files exist will either break them or, worse, have them broken for it by whoever merges next.

SMALLER, STILL WORTH FIXING BEFORE THIS IS HANDED OUT: the `main.ts:1005` evidence `quote` is fabricated code that exists nowhere in the repo (self-flagged, paraphrase accurate — but replace it, that is the S120 failure in miniature); the claim that gathererOrders.test.ts:132 goes RED is wrong — it goes VACUOUSLY GREEN and silently stops testing the Council fix, which a session will read as "no action needed"; "abandons the queue entirely" overstates it, because `consumeGathererOrder` still pops on a lucky type match; the perf note undercounts (three freeSparks passes on the preempt path, not two); and SPARK_CANON.md + src/canon.test.ts must come out of file_set — I grepped both and neither contains a single gatherer or queue assertion, so they are pure collision surface.

NO CANON RULING IS BROKEN. Owner ruling B4 (priority override, never an on/off switch) survives the fix intact, which I verified by tracing gathererOrders.test.ts:193 through the proposed logic. §1's four archived subsystems and §9b's retaliation-kiting DO-NOT-FIX are untouched. The stat ladder is not involved — this change subtracts no damage and creates no pool.
